title: Choose the visual world for the DP Interactive rebuild
question: The roll assigned Coastal Travel Editorial. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Coastal Travel Editorial
options.lineage: Luxury coffee-table travel & hospitality publishing — Cereal, Condé Nast Traveler property spreads, Aman/Six Senses brand books
options.thesis: The development as a beautifully art-directed property spread that happens to be fully interactive and three-dimensional.
options.viewport: A full-bleed cinematic aerial hero of the Ghazala Bay coastline, a masthead-style serif title (“Zoya — Ghazala Bay”) fading in like a magazine cover line, one gold-foil caption plate naming the view; the globe-to-region-to-project camera move plays like turning a spread rather than a generic zoom.
options.risk: Reads like a static brochure if editorial restraint isn't paired with continuous camera motion and real interactivity — motion and depth have to carry as much weight as the photography.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: vernacular ephemera — mid-century airline ticket wallets, carbon-copy coupons, route maps
options.thesis: The layered journey (location → masterplan → building → unit) staged as a coupon book: each stage a leg you tear off in sequence.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with the journey's staged structure and its travel/aspiration register suits a coastal vacation property — but its coupon model is literally irreversible (“used = void”), which fights a product that needs free, repeated exploration. Loses on product clarity.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.lineage: signals & instruments — amber-lit photographic darkroom, timed development baths
options.thesis: Construction progress and before/after staged as a photograph slowly developing under amber safelight.
options.case: Beautiful, specific fit for the Compare/Progress feature alone — the ‘image emerging from nothing’ reveal is worth stealing as a transition detail. But its fixed, linear station sequence and moody near-black palette can't carry free map navigation, filters, or a luxury-aspirational register across the whole surface. Loses on product clarity at full scale.

options.label: WebGL Shader Portal
options.lineage: experiential-studio web design — full-screen fragment-shader scenes, thin type over living pixels
options.thesis: A living, breathing full-screen shader field with the interface floating as thin type over it — the literal ‘modern tech, wow effect’ read.
options.case: Delivers spectacle and real web leverage, but an abstract color field can't carry real aerial photography, a real 3D masterplan, or real construction photos as substance — it becomes decoration the product's actual content has to fight through. Loses on product clarity; also the closest of the six to the generic AI-interface calibration risk (dark ground, single neon accent).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The interactive-masterplan category default, executed at full craft: a tidy map-plus-sidebar layout, translucent glass info panels, blue accent, clean sans UI over the map canvas.
canonCard.viewport: Filters left, 3D map center, glass panel slides in on selection with blue-accented buttons and icons — the PropTech-dashboard look most competitors ship.
